title: Scholarship and Mixtape
premise: Cyrus Joubert, a scholarship student and anonymous whistleblower coder at elite Ashford Prep, has spent senior year documenting the school's corrupt donor pipeline while counting down to graduation. When a group chat called ORACLE begins posting predictions that come true with impossible accuracy, Cyrus realizes it's running on her own leaked data — someone stole her archive and weaponized it. As the predictions turn from pranks to targeted destruction, she must unmask the person using her code for revenge before her own identity as the whistleblower is exposed, choosing between protecting the boy she loves (the headmaster's son) and burning the whole rotten system down. In the end, Cyrus releases everything on her own terms during graduation, sacrificing her scholarship future but freeing herself from every label the school ever gave her.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former private-school scholarship kid who spent four years learning how institutions protect themselves. They write stories about clever outsiders who refuse to play by rules written against them.

chapters.title: Countdown Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Opening day of spring semester: Cyrus maps her 112 days to graduation like a prison sentence, coding her anonymous exposé account 'MOTH' between classes. We see her double life — perfect scholarship student by day, digital ghost by night. Emotional beat: weary defiance, the comfort of a plan.

chapters.title: The First Prediction
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A group chat called ORACLE adds her without permission and posts a prediction: the gym floods overnight. It happens exactly as described. Cyrus recognizes a fragment of her own code in the message formatting. Emotional beat: cold dread — someone knows who she is.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Theo Ashcombe, the headmaster's son. Theo defends Cyrus when a teacher accuses her of the flood prank; their charged history simmers beneath polite distance. Cyrus notices he's also in ORACLE — added, not joined. Emotional beat: attraction sharpened by mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Archive Breach
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She audits her encrypted archive and finds it was copied months ago through a compromised library terminal. The theft window narrows to eleven people. Emotional beat: violation — her secret self handled by stranger's hands.

chapters.title: Prediction Two
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. ORACLE predicts a beloved teacher's resignation before the teacher knows herself. The chat's tone shifts from eerie fun to menace. Theo starts his own quiet investigation to protect his father's reputation. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to crack against evidence.

chapters.title: The Donor List
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback chapter: how Cyrus built MOTH after her brother's scholarship was revoked to cover a trustee's embezzlement. Her motive crystallizes for readers. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Rooftop Truce
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus and Theo, both hunting ORACLE separately, catch each other mid-investigation and form an uneasy alliance on the library roof. Almost-kiss interrupted by a new prediction naming Cyrus herself. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming inside paranoia.

chapters.title: What ORACLE Knows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The prediction about her arrives early: 'MOTH speaks on May 30th.' Only her real identity could know that date. She realizes ORACLE isn't predicting the future — it's scheduling it. Emotional beat: terror converting to fury.

chapters.title: Eleven Suspects
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus and Theo build a suspect board: the janitor with IT certs, the rival valedictorian, the admissions officer, Theo's father among them. Each alibi holds except one — quiet scholarship kid Wren, whose terminal access fits perfectly. Emotional beat: the ugliness of suspicion.

chapters.title: Midterm Massacre
chapters.summary: Wren's POV introduced. ORACLE leaks exam answers to half the school, then exposes who used them — engineered chaos. Wren watches Cyrus investigate and we learn Wren admires MOTH obsessively. Emotional beat: hero worship curdling into something possessive.

chapters.title: Duty's Price
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father reveals he's known about MOTH for months and offers a deal: help identify the leaker quietly, and Cyrus's scholarship stays safe. Theo must choose family or Cyrus. Emotional beat: love against duty, first true cost.

chapters.title: The Trap
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus plants false data in her archive like poisoned bait, seeding different lies to each suspect. Within days, one version surfaces in ORACLE. The trap works — too well. Emotional beat: hunter's triumph shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confronted, Wren confesses partially: they found MOTH's archive abandoned on a wiped drive and believed continuing the work was destiny, not theft. But Wren swears the violent predictions aren't theirs. Someone else has access. Emotional beat: sympathy for the devil you understand.

chapters.title: Third Hand
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus and Theo trace the second intruder: someone inside the administration feeding ORACLE institutional secrets. The predictions are a cover for something bigger — a hostile takeover of the board timed to graduation week. Emotional beat: scale shift, personal mystery becomes systemic war.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus is summoned before the disciplinary committee on fabricated charges — the takeover faction flushing out MOTH. Theo testifies ambiguously, saving her expulsion but betraying his father openly. Emotional beat: sacrifice made visible; love declared under oath.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Plan
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father disowns his protection; Theo loses his inheritance and his name's safety net. He shows up soaked at Cyrus's door with nothing but a flash drive of board documents he stole back. Emotional beat: two people with nothing left but each other and the truth.

chapters.title: The Real Oracle
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Unmasking: the mastermind is the admissions officer who revoked her brother's scholarship — she's been using MOTH's stolen archive to blackmail trustees into installing her as head. She offers Cyrus partnership: join me, keep your future. Emotional beat: temptation offered by the villain of her origin story.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cyrus declines — justice outside the law can't become power over people. With Wren's coding help and Theo's documents, they prepare to release everything: the corruption AND the manipulation, including their own complicity. Emotional beat: resolve hardened into clarity.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The mastermind strikes first, locking them out, framing Wren for everything. Wren takes the fall publicly to buy Cyrus time, whispering 'finish it.' Emotional beat: redemption through sacrifice; the least likely hero.

chapters.title: May 30th
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax. At graduation, as diplomas are handed out, Cyrus hijacks the auditorium screens and releases the full archive live — the corruption, the manipulation, her own name as MOTH. Chaos, then silence, then students standing. Emotional beat: the sentence served ends in liberation, not punishment.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fallout: investigations launched, the mastermind arrested, Ashford's board dissolved. Theo and Cyrus, both expelled-adjacent and free, sit on the library roof one last time. Labels gone, futures unwritten. Emotional beat: tender uncertainty as a gift.

chapters.title: Mixtape
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue. Months later, Cyrus gets an email from Wren — released, rebuilding, sending a mixtape of songs 'for the girl who finished it.' Cyrus presses play on a train leaving town, no return address, no title but her own name. Emotional beat: open-hearted ending; she decides who she is now.
